extracted.intended_audience: prospective Guggenheim Fellowship applicants (artists, writers, scholars, scientists) and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation fellowship program: who it supports and the program's priorities — intended to inform prospective applicants about the fellowship's purpose, scope, and nature of selection. Not an application form or scoring rubric, but states programmatic criteria and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships for exceptional individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation offers fellowships to exceptional individuals in pursuit of scholarship in any field of knowledge and creation in any art form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the program's primary eligibility/selection framing: candidates are expected to be "exceptional." The page illustrates this with prominent past Fellows (e.g., Jennifer Doudna, Romare Bearden, Roxane Gay, Dorothea Lange) as exemplars of the caliber the Foundation supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of study / artistic field scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are offered "in any field of knowledge and creation in any art form."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation supports work across more than 50 fields of study; there are no narrow disciplinary restrictions on the types of scholarship or creative practice that may be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the fellowship: pursuit of scholarship and creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships support individuals "in pursuit of scholarship in any field of knowledge and creation in any art form."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is intended to enable recipients to pursue their work (scholarship or creative projects). The site emphasizes that donations directly fund Fellowships that enable artists, writers, scholars, and scientists to pursue their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support under the freest possible conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are awarded to enable work "under the freest possible conditions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language signals that the Foundation intends to impose minimal constraints on how Fellows use their time and funds, prioritizing creative and scholarly freedom rather than prescriptive project requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of significant/transformative contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: For 100 years, Guggenheim Fellows have made world-changing contributions to more than 50 fields of study, reshaping our culture and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not an explicit numeric scoring criterion, the page frames Fellows as people whose work has broad, lasting impact — implying selection favors demonstrated achievement or potential for transformative contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing affiliation: "Once a Fellow, Always a Fellow"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stated principle indicates a lasting relationship between awardees and the Foundation. It is programmatic/policy language rather than an application-evaluation criterion, but it signals the Foundation's long-term commitment to Fellows.
